questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

People like pictures of the savanna, even if they have never been there. In one study, people of different ages ①<u>looked</u> at images of tropical forests, deserts, and the East African savanna. Since none of these people had visited savannas, the implication is that this preference was ②<u>programmed</u> into their brains. As people get older, this preference gets ③<u>modified</u> by where they have lived. Researchers showed that young children in Austria prefer landscapes thinly ④<u>dotting</u> with trees and with low mountains, scenes that ⑤<u>resemble</u> the savanna.
questions.explanation: ④ landscapes가 '나무로 점점이 채워진' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 dotted가 되어야 한다(thinly dotted with trees). 능동의 현재분사 dotting은 틀리다. ①주어 people에 대한 과거동사 looked, ②be동사+과거분사 수동 programmed, ③get+과거분사 modified, ⑤scenes를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사 뒤 복수동사 resemble은 모두 적절. [출처: 수능특강 영어 28강 1번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

Dreamers find it difficult to determine whether a memory is from a dream or some other source after time has passed, ①<u>knowing</u> as 'source monitoring.' It is difficult to distinguish between memories of real dreams and made-up ones. Dream source monitoring was found to be ②<u>less</u> accurate than other memory source monitoring. Although dreams are usually more vivid than imagination, the cognitive operations that ③<u>generate</u> imagining are also remembered. Dream generation, in contrast, is 'transparent' in that we don't experience the generation process, ④<u>making</u> it more difficult to source monitor and ⑤<u>distinguish</u> from reality.
questions.explanation: ① 앞의 내용 전체를 받아 '출처 점검이라 알려진'의 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 known이 되어야 한다(분사구문). 능동의 현재분사 knowing은 틀리다. ②비교급 less, ③주격 관계대명사 that 뒤 동사 generate, ④분사구문 making, ⑤to source monitor에 병렬로 이어지는 (to) distinguish는 모두 적절. [출처: 수능특강 영어 28강 2번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

Much research in social psychology has documented some of the key strategies ①<u>that</u> people rely upon in defending the belief 'I am good.' For example, when people perform poorly at something, they tend to trivialize their failures. This trivialization disarms those failures and prevents them from ②<u>overwriting</u> their life stories. Imagine, say, ③<u>which</u> someone fails a calculus test. A common defensive response is to conclude that this test was just not that important to them. By titrating how importantly people view their successes and failures, they can shape their emotional reactions to these events in a way ④<u>that</u> enables them to tell a more convincing story ⑤<u>that</u> 'I am good.'
questions.explanation: ③ 뒤에 완전한 절(someone fails a calculus test)이 이어지고 Imagine의 목적어 명사절을 이끄므로 접속사 that이 되어야 한다. 관계대명사 which는 틀리다. ①strategies를 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사 that, ②전치사 from의 목적어 동명사 overwriting, ④a way를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that, ⑤story와 동격을 이루는 접속사 that은 모두 적절. [출처: 수능특강 영어 28강 3번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

Teaching reflects what society itself demands; it necessitates that disorder — of students and teachers alike — ①<u>yield</u> to its opposite. Effective teaching requires that, ②<u>failing</u> their own self-imposed order, students experience the imposition of some outer order so that inner order may develop. This means in practice that the goals of classes ③<u>be</u> clearly set, that the manner of achieving them be clear, and that all activities ④<u>be</u> directed somehow to their attainment. Above all, it implies structured industry — study and activity that ⑤<u>is</u> oriented toward a goal and pursued with perseverance.
questions.explanation: ⑤ 선행사 study and activity가 복수이므로 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤 동사는 복수형 are가 되어야 한다. 단수 is는 틀리다. ①necessitates that 뒤 (should)yield, ②분사구문 failing, ③④requires/means that 뒤 (should)be로 모두 원형은 적절. [출처: 수능특강 영어 25강 1번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

Not too much or too little — that's what moderation means. Moderation does not mean that you have to eliminate low-nutrient-density foods from your diet, such as soft drinks and candy, but rather that you ①<u>can include</u> them occasionally. You probably ②<u>have heard</u> that vitamin C has positive effects, but that doesn't mean huge doses of this essential nutrient are appropriate for you. The body needs zinc for hundreds of chemical reactions, including ③<u>those</u> that support normal growth. Too much zinc, however, can cause deficiency of copper, another essential mineral, which can ④<u>leading</u> to damaged immune function. Being moderate means that you do not restrict any one type of food, but rather that all types ⑤<u>can fit</u> into a healthful diet.
questions.explanation: ④ 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 lead가 되어야 한다. 현재분사 leading은 틀리다. ①조동사+원형 can include, ②현재완료 have heard, ③앞의 reactions를 대신하는 지시대명사 those, ⑤조동사+원형 can fit은 모두 적절. [출처: 수능특강 영어 30강 1번]

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Pre-Consumer Waste is waste that is generated by the industrial processes used to make the products or packaging that we buy as consumers. This is manufacturing waste and is typically very clean, of consistent quality and comprises only a single material. Examples are offcuts from making aluminium cans, cardboard boxes, or textile offcuts from making furniture. Such waste was in the past often sent for disposal, but increasingly producers are recycling their internal waste to save money by turning unwanted trimmings or offcuts back into useable raw materials. To send such materials for disposal is not only poor financial practice by the producer; from an environmental perspective it is criminal. These are good-quality, clean and easily collectable materials that just happen to be ______.
choices: ① too contaminated by mixed substances to reuse
② produced in quantities too small to recover
③ in the wrong form rather than truly worthless
④ demanded more by consumers than by producers
⑤ regulated too strictly for industrial recycling
questions.explanation: 빈칸 앞에서 pre-consumer 폐기물은 깨끗하고 균질하며 단일 소재라 양질의 원료로 되돌릴 수 있다고 강조한다. 따라서 이 자재들은 '쓸모없는 것이 아니라 단지 잘못된 형태에 있을 뿐'이라는 ③이 정답. ①'혼합 오염'·②'양이 너무 적음'은 본문의 'clean·single material' 진술과 반대, ④소비자 수요·⑤규제는 글의 초점(재활용 가치)과 무관. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(5월 35)]

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Classical works by playwrights such as Shakespeare or even American musical song lyrics contain unconventional methods of communicating characters' thoughts, and take more skill and patience to understand. The reader must be mindful not to let the poetic form or archaic word usage get in the way, but instead see the form itself as a revealing stylistic technique. Musical theater pieces are particularly difficult to visualize when reading because of the diminished emphasis on dialogue and a significant emphasis on song and dance. For example, when the music and lyrics are removed from a musical theater script, what is left is the dialogue, known as the book or libretto, and it can be very thin. There is an emphasis on dance, movement, or action that can be time-consuming when performed on stage, but ______ when typed into a play script.
choices: ① can take very little space
questions.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 무대 상연 시 많은 시간이 드는 춤·동작이 '대본에 글로 옮겨지면' 어떻게 되는지를 대조한다. 앞서 가사·음악을 빼면 대본(libretto)이 매우 빈약해진다고 했으므로, 글로는 '아주 적은 공간만 차지한다'는 ①이 정답. ②리허설·④무대비용·⑤배우 혼란은 'typed into a script(지면)'라는 대조 축과 무관, ③감정 강도는 본문에 없는 비약. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 30)]

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

In humans, the infant immune system is less active than that of adults, enabling a wide range of bacteria to establish in our guts. Similarly, young plants release fewer defensive compounds into the soil than older ones, allowing a broad variety of microbes to colonize their rhizospheres. Human breast milk contains sugars that babies can't digest; it now seems their sole purpose is to feed the bacteria with which the child will grow. Similarly, young plants release large quantities of sugars into the soil to feed their new microbiomes. Just as the bacteria in our guts outcompete invading pathogens, the microbes in the rhizosphere create a defensive ring around the root. In both cases, the host actively ______ in order to be protected from disease.
choices: ① eliminates all microbial life early on
② nurtures beneficial microbes that suppress pathogens
③ strengthens its own cells without outside help
④ delays immune development until adulthood
⑤ relies on chemical defenses rather than microbes
questions.explanation: 본문은 인간의 장과 식물의 뿌리권이 평행하게, 숙주가 당분을 내어 유익균을 길러 그 유익균이 병원균을 억제·공격하게 한다는 구조를 반복한다. 따라서 빈칸은 '병원균을 억제하는 유익균을 기른다'는 ②가 정답. ①'모든 미생물 제거'·⑤'미생물 대신 화학 방어'는 본문 논지와 정반대, ③'외부 도움 없이'·④'면역 발달 지연'은 미생물 공생이라는 핵심과 어긋남. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(5월 30)]

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles. These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon called vortex shedding.

(A) The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining. To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in their powers to confuse the wind.

(B) As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, where eventually it separates from the face of the structure. The difference in pressures on the front and back faces gives rise to vortices, spinning currents of wind that flow downstream.

(C) Orienting the building so that the longer face is parallel with prevailing winds can help. Chopping or rounding off corners can likewise make it more aerodynamic, and roughing up the corners through balconies or stepped corners disturbs the formation of strong vortices.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글(사각형 빌딩이 vortex shedding 유발) → (B)바람이 빌딩에 부딪혀 와류가 생기는 과정 → (A)그 와류가 빌딩을 위험하게 흔들어 설계자들이 바람을 교란하려 함 → (C)구체적 방법(방향 배치·모서리 깎기) 순서. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C)인 ③이 정답. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 38)]

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Speakers don't always put everything that's important to them into words. Very often you can understand a speaker's meaning by observing their nonverbal behaviors such as a change in vocal tone or volume, eye contact, facial expressions and gestures.

(A) As it is easy to misinterpret nonverbal behavior, effective listeners verbally confirm their interpretations of someone's nonverbal communication. A question as simple as 'You seem upset — am I reading that right?' can prevent misunderstanding.

(B) If, as nonverbal research indicates, more than half of a speaker's meaning is conveyed nonverbally, we are missing a lot of important information if we fail to attend to it.

(C) Even Freud suggested that no mortal can keep a secret: if his lips are silent, he chatters with his fingertips. No wonder it is difficult for most people to conceal what they mean and feel in a face-to-face discussion.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글(말보다 비언어로 의미 파악) → (A)비언어는 오해하기 쉬우니 듣는 이가 말로 확인한다(예시) → (B)의미의 절반 이상이 비언어로 전달되므로 놓치면 정보 손실 → (C)Freud 인용으로 숨길 수 없음을 강조하며 마무리. 따라서 (A)-(B)-(C)인 ①이 정답. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 32)]

questions.question:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Imagination continues to function when perception is not actively discerning objects, in cases of emotion, disease, and sleep.

(A) In such cases, a small similarity between a perceived object and the thing one expects to see can lead to the misidentification of the perceived object as that thing. The coward sees the enemy, while the lover sees the object of desire everywhere.

(B) Emotions dispose one to see the world in a distorted way. A coward's perceptual disposition is affected by his disposition to experience fear, and a lover's expectations are affected by desire.

(C) The more affected one is, the less similarity is required for the thing to appear. While the central organ of sense normally functions by comparing similarities and differences, emotions dispose one to discern objects inaccurately.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글(감정·질병·수면 시 상상이 작동) → (B)감정이 세계를 왜곡해 보게 함(겁쟁이·연인 예) → (A)'In such cases' 그런 경우 작은 유사성이 오인을 부른다(구체 예) → (C)정도가 심할수록 유사성이 덜 필요하다는 일반화. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C)인 ③이 정답. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 33)]

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?

Plants have evolved defenses almost as diverse as the number of genera. ① Some load their tissues with harsh compounds that are unpleasant to insects or intoxicate them, encouraging the insects to go bother another plant. ② Structural defenses like thick coats of wax on leaves may prevent some insect species from damaging the plant tissues altogether. ③ The global market for ornamental houseplants has grown rapidly as urban consumers seek greenery for their apartments. ④ Nor are individual plants entirely on their own while under attack; plants can release chemical compounds that let their same-species neighbors know that an attack is likely coming. ⑤ These cues push nearby plants to start building up defensive compounds in their tissues before the insects arrive.
questions.explanation: 글은 식물이 진화시킨 다양한 방어(화학물질·구조적 방어·이웃에 보내는 경고 신호)를 다룬다. ③'장식용 관엽식물의 시장 성장'은 도시 소비와 원예 시장 얘기로 식물의 방어 기제 논지와 무관. ①②는 개별 방어, ④⑤는 이웃 식물 경고로 모두 흐름에 부합. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 36)]

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?

Although there may be elements that trigger instinctive response, spectacle works primarily within a cultural frame and is subject to prevailing modes of perception that observers bring to bear. ① In saying that, we stress that creation of spectacle is not a universal expression of culture, but a strategy commonly used by people from many cultures to address specific needs. ② Modern cinema relies heavily on digital technology that did not exist a century ago. ③ The task of creating spectacle has been likened to creating new works of literature, where writers feel bound by the rules of their genre yet need to show originality to impress their audiences. ④ By extension, spectacle is produced by working within established conventions while introducing enough novelty to capture attention. ⑤ Thus spectacle, like literature, balances cultural tradition against the demand for fresh, striking effects.
questions.explanation: 글은 스펙터클이 문화적 틀 안에서 작동하며, 문학 창작처럼 전통(관습)과 독창성의 균형으로 만들어진다는 논지다. ②'현대 영화가 한 세기 전엔 없던 디지털 기술에 의존한다'는 기술사 얘기로 전통-독창성 균형이라는 논지와 무관. ①③④⑤는 모두 스펙터클과 문학의 유비·균형 흐름. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 37)]

questions.question:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?

Dietary behaviors are, in large part, the consequence of automatic responses to a particular situation with food, many of which lead to increased caloric consumption. ① Regular aerobic exercise strengthens the heart and lowers the risk of cardiovascular disease over time. ② Individuals are subject to inherent cognitive limitations and mostly lack the capacity to consistently resist contextual cues that encourage eating. ③ Take going to the movies: for many, a night at the movies also means sharing popcorn, candy, and soda that people cannot resist. ④ Another example is eating potato chips or peanuts set out during a card game, consumed not because of hunger but because of the social environment. ⑤ Grocery stores likewise use the placement of items to encourage impulse buying prompted by the surroundings.
questions.explanation: 글은 식이 행동이 환경·상황 단서에 대한 자동적 반응(영화관 간식·사교 모임 간식·마트 진열)이라는 논지다. ①'규칙적 유산소 운동이 심장을 강화한다'는 운동의 건강 효과로 '환경 단서에 의한 자동적 섭취'라는 논지와 무관. ②인지적 한계, ③④환경이 유발하는 섭취 사례, ⑤마트 진열은 모두 흐름에 부합. [출처: 수능특강 영어 30강 2번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

Ever since the early Enlightenment, preservation and conservation have been closely related. Taken as near synonyms, their meaning is to maintain an object or system in its present state, to protect it from change. Conservationists who distinguish their activities from preservation emphasize conservation's restorative aspects — restoring a historical instrument, a painting, or an ecosystem. Conservationists acknowledge change but try to manage it in order to prolong a desired state. Preservationists think of themselves more as protectors; they criticize conservationists for prioritizing yield or use, rather than interfering as minimally as possible to preserve the original object or system.
choices: ① the economic value of restoring historical artifacts
② techniques for preventing damage to ecosystems
③ the historical origins of the Enlightenment idea of nature
④ why preservation has replaced conservation over time
⑤ the contrast between conservation and preservation in managing change
questions.explanation: 글은 보전(conservation)과 보존(preservation)을 대비하며, 전자는 변화를 관리해 원하는 상태를 늘리려 하고 후자는 최소 개입으로 원형을 지키려 한다는 차이를 설명한다. 따라서 주제는 '변화 관리에서 보전과 보존의 대비'인 ⑤. ①경제적 가치·②생태계 보호 기법은 지엽, ③계몽주의 기원·④대체는 본문에 없는 비약. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 31)]

questions.question:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

The dependent and shifting nature of art values, not only on the market but inherently, is uppermost in the mind of today's art collector. Acquiring a work is acquiring a piece of art history, or it is acquiring nothing beyond an object of personal enjoyment. In signing his check the collector asserts his belief in the future presence of the work as a significant point attained by art. History, however, is open to anything, and the merit of the chosen painting has at best only the validation of a present-day consensus — a consensus all but certain to be displaced. In the last analysis, committing himself to a painting is the collector's own act, by which he affirms his aesthetic judgment and the conviction that he can predict where art is going.
choices: ① the financial risks of investing in the modern art market
② the collector's bet on uncertain, shifting artistic value
③ the role of museums in preserving art history
④ how consensus among critics determines fair prices
⑤ the personal pleasure of owning beautiful objects
questions.explanation: 글은 예술 가치가 본래 가변적·의존적이어서 현재의 합의조차 곧 뒤집히는데도, 수집가가 '예술이 갈 방향을 예측할 수 있다'는 확신으로 불확실한 가치에 자신을 거는 행위를 다룬다. 따라서 주제는 '불확실하고 변하는 예술 가치에 대한 수집가의 베팅'인 ②. ①투자 위험·④비평가 합의·가격은 지엽, ③미술관·⑤개인적 즐거움은 본문이 부차로 언급하거나 부정한 요소. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 34)]

questions.question:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

When we lecture, scold, yell, or criticize, or when we say something positive in a sarcastic tone, it activates children's amygdala, triggering their stress response and putting them into a defensive, rigid state. When we say no or don't, it releases stress chemicals in their brains associated with fear and anger. Functional brain imaging shows that even seeing the word no on a screen for less than a second causes the brain to release dozens of stress-producing hormones. Conversely, positive words like yes, love, and peace activate systems in the prefrontal cortex related to emotional regulation. The problem is that negative words like no and don't have a more powerful effect on kids than positive words.
choices: ① the powerful neural impact of negative words on children
② effective discipline strategies for managing classrooms
③ how MRI scanners measure brain activity in real time
④ the benefits of teaching children a positive vocabulary
⑤ why children misbehave when criticized by adults
questions.explanation: 글은 꾸짖음·부정어가 아이의 편도체를 자극해 스트레스 호르몬을 분비시키고, 부정어가 긍정어보다 뇌에 더 강력한 영향을 준다는 신경학적 사실을 설명한다. 따라서 주제는 '부정어가 아이에게 미치는 강력한 신경적 영향'인 ①. ②훈육 전략·④긍정 어휘 교육은 처방으로 본문 초점(영향 자체)과 다르고, ③MRI 측정·⑤비행 원인은 지엽. [출처: 수능특강 영어 25강 2번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

According to British economist Lionel Robbins, whether goods and services are beneficial to human welfare or not, economics should study them if they satisfy the wants of some men. Economics does not deal with what ends should be achieved — what wants should be satisfied and what not — because in this regard man himself has to decide. Economics itself does not make a choice; the economist only tells in what ways the given ends can be achieved with the minimum possible resources. Whether the ends chosen by man are good or bad, noble or ignoble, economics should study them, because the task of the economist is not to praise or criticise but only to analyse and explain. Therefore, according to Robbins, economics is neutral between ends.
choices: ① Economics: The Science of Maximizing Human Welfare
② How Economists Decide Which Wants Are Worthwhile
③ The Moral Duty of Economics to Judge Human Ends
④ Economics as a Neutral Science Between Competing Ends
⑤ Why Scarce Resources Force Us to Rank Our Desires
questions.explanation: 글은 로빈스의 견해로, 경제학은 목적의 좋고 나쁨을 판단하지 않고 주어진 목적을 최소 자원으로 달성하는 방법만 분석하므로 '목적들 사이에서 중립적'이라고 결론짓는다. 따라서 제목은 '목적들 사이에서 중립적인 과학으로서의 경제학'인 ④. ②경제학자가 욕구를 판단·③도덕적 판단 의무는 본문이 명시적으로 부정한 내용, ①복지 극대화·⑤희소성 순위는 지엽·비약. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(5월 32)]

questions.question:
다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

The experiences of learning to ride a bicycle or drive a car illustrate how the 'what' and 'how' systems interact. When we learn to drive, each required action — looking in the mirror, signaling, pressing the clutch — is explicitly thought of and double-checked. Once learned, the required actions become second nature, performed without explicit thinking; information is perceived directly. If you start to think too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport confirm that self-consciousness is one's worst enemy: tennis, golf, or billiard players report that they lose their 'touch' by thinking too much about their moves.
choices: ① The First Steps in Learning to Drive Safely
② When Thinking Too Much Gets in the Way of Skill
③ How the Brain Identifies Objects on the Road
④ Why Beginners Make More Mistakes Than Experts
⑤ The Physical Benefits of Practicing a Sport Daily
questions.explanation: 글은 익힌 기술이 의식적 사고 없이 자동으로 수행되며, 오히려 지나치게 의식하면 수행이 무너진다(운전 사고·운동선수의 'touch' 상실)는 점을 강조한다. 따라서 제목은 '지나친 생각이 숙련을 방해할 때'인 ②. ①운전 입문·③뇌의 사물 인식·④초보의 실수는 지엽이거나 부분, ⑤운동의 신체적 효과는 무관. [출처: 수능특강 영어 25강 3번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The bigger someone is, the more damage they can do to themselves through even a relatively innocuous accident. Despite toddlers falling over regularly, the injuries they sustain are rarely serious: their relatively thick bones in comparison to their mass mean they rarely build up enough energy to do themselves much damage. Adults falling over impact the ground with a much larger force because of their increased mass. The nonlinear relationship between mass and bone strength means that although adults' bones are thicker than a toddler's in absolute terms, they may not be relatively thick enough to compensate for the larger impact. For the same reasons, taller people suffer more fall-related injuries like hip breaks than shorter people.

[요약문] As body size increases, the impact force of a fall grows __(A)__ than bone strength does, so larger people are __(B)__ to serious fall injuries.
choices: ③ (A) at the same rate … (B) equally prone
questions.explanation: 체격이 클수록 낙상 충격력은 뼈 강도보다 더 빠르게(비선형으로) 커지므로(faster), 큰 사람일수록 심각한 낙상 부상에 더 취약하다(more prone). 따라서 (A) faster, (B) more prone인 ⑤가 정답. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 35)]

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Through stories we can explore the human condition and see how other people think. Regardless of the language, there is something universal about what occurs in the brain when we process narratives, triggering better self-awareness and empathy. Psychologists scanned people listening to narratives in English, Farsi, and Mandarin, and found the same patterns of brain activation. And the more absorbed in a story a reader is, the more empathetically they behave: those 'highly absorbed' in a story were about twice as likely to help pick up dropped pens. Another study concluded that literary fiction uniquely engages the processes needed to access characters' subjective experiences — if you read novels, you can probably read emotions, vital skills for cooperative societies.

[요약문] Engaging deeply with narratives activates universal brain processes that __(A)__ empathy, which in turn supports __(B)__ behavior in real life.
questions.explanation: 글은 서사 처리가 언어와 무관하게 공감을 높이고(enhance), 이야기에 몰입한 사람일수록 현실에서 더 돕는 협력적 행동을 보인다고 한다. 따라서 (A) enhance, (B) cooperative인 ⑤가 정답. [출처: 수능특강 영어 26강 3번]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

The autonomy granted to the individual in terms of free speech can be both individual and relational in nature. The individual's speech must be ①<u>protected</u> in order to allow them to freely develop their personality. This is important, even bearing in mind that this development is only possible in social life, in relation to and in cooperation with others. Relational autonomy, however, also takes the interests of the audience into account. Speech can also ②<u>limit</u> the autonomy of others, for example in cases of defamation, invasion of privacy, or hate speech. European legal systems take this aspect into account when setting the limits of freedom of expression, ③<u>restricting</u> it in the interests of the autonomy of those ④<u>affected</u> by the speech, in order to ⑤<u>endanger</u> the peace and security of social coexistence.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장은 표현의 자유를 제한하는 목적이 사회적 공존의 평화와 안전을 '보장(ensure)'하기 위함이므로, '위태롭게 하다'는 ⑤ endanger는 문맥상 정반대로 부적절하다(ensure가 맞다). ①protected, ②limit, ③restricting, ④affected는 모두 문맥에 맞다. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(5월 36)]

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

For thousands of years in the West, red was the only color worthy of that name, the only ①<u>true</u> color. As much on the historical as hierarchical level, it ②<u>fell short of</u> all others. Not that other colors did not exist, but they had to wait a long time before they were considered colors and played a comparable role in material culture and systems of thought. It was with red that humans did their first color ③<u>experiments</u>, achieved their first successes, and then constructed a chromatic universe. It was within the range of reds that they learned early on to ④<u>diversify</u> the palette and produce varied tones and shades, as the oldest known color terms ⑤<u>demonstrate</u>.
questions.explanation: red가 역사적·위계적으로 다른 모든 색을 '능가했다(exceeded)'는 맥락이므로, '~에 못 미쳤다'는 ② fell short of는 정반대로 부적절하다. ①true(유일한 진정한 색), ③experiments(최초의 색 실험), ④diversify(팔레트 다양화), ⑤demonstrate(색 용어가 입증)는 모두 적절. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 39)]

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장] By lowering the cost of data collection, mining, and analysis, however, AI can help offset these imbalances.

In the pharmaceutical industry, algorithms are being employed to find treatments for rare diseases that haven't received much attention. ( ① ) The hard truth has always been that pharma devotes more research resources to diseases that affect the rich. ( ② ) The definition of 'rare' has too often been associated with 'poor' — even if a disease is prevalent in a population that cannot afford to pay for it, it has been neglected compared to First World illnesses. ( ③ ) Historically, then, commercial incentives have directed attention away from diseases of the poor. ( ④ ) We see the democratizing power of AI to broaden the attention of the medical and research communities to traditionally neglected health issues and populations. ( ⑤ )
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 'however, AI가 데이터 비용을 낮춰 이 불균형(상업적 유인이 빈자의 병을 외면해 온 것)을 상쇄한다'는 전환이다. ③ 앞까지 상업적 유인이 빈자의 병을 외면해 온 문제가 서술되고, ④ 자리에 'AI가 불균형을 상쇄'가 들어가면 바로 뒤 'AI의 민주화하는 힘' 문장과 자연스럽게 이어진다. 따라서 정답은 ④. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 40)]

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

The structure of glass is, frankly, a bit of a mess. Clear and perfect as it might appear, at the molecular level glass looks more like a random ball-pit of atoms. In theory it's both liquid and solid, though in practice it behaves as a solid. At room temperature glass never behaves as a liquid, even an imperceptibly viscous one, even over long periods. Those misshapen sheets of glass in old stained-glass windows, thicker at the bottom, are generally not that way because the glass is slowly sinking; unless the church has endured temperatures over 400°C, they are uneven because that's the way they were blown and solidified in the first place. Flat glass was only developed in the nineteenth century, and truly flat, thin sheets had to wait until the middle of the twentieth century. The paradox is that, despite being one of the oldest human-made substances, scientists still struggle to comprehend why glass behaves as it does.
choices: ① 분자 수준에서 유리는 무질서한 원자 배열로 보인다.
② 실온에서 유리는 점성이 매우 큰 액체로도 행동하지 않는다.
③ 오래된 스테인드글라스의 두께 차이는 제작 당시의 성형 방식 때문이다.
④ 평평한 판유리는 20세기 초에 처음으로 개발되었다.
⑤ 유리는 가장 오래된 인공 물질 중 하나이지만 그 거동은 아직 완전히 이해되지 않았다.
questions.explanation: 본문은 평판 유리(flat glass)가 19세기에 개발되었고 진정으로 평평하고 얇은 판유리는 20세기 중반에야 가능했다고 한다. 따라서 '20세기 초에 처음 개발'이라는 ④는 본문과 불일치. ①무질서한 원자, ②실온에서 액체로 행동 안 함, ③제작 당시 성형 방식, ⑤가장 오래된 물질이나 미해명은 모두 본문과 일치. [출처: 5·6월 모의고사(6월 41)]
